outcome: Mother's Level of Childbirth Satisfaction Rating Scale
cohort: Two hundred and twenty pregnant women were divided into an experimental group receiving doula services and a control group receiving routine hospital care.
finding: The doula program did not significantly reduce anxiety or postnatal depression, but it led to a statistically significant reduction in the cesarean section rate and an increase in the normal spontaneous delivery rate.
mod_finding: The doula group exhibited a statistically significant reduction in the cesarean section (C/S) rate (13.0% vs. 43.2%) and an increase in the normal spontaneous delivery (NSD) rate (87.0% vs. 56.8%) compared to the control group.
followup_time: Data collected during the postpartum hospitalization period
